title: Stars & galaxies
examples: How big is the Milky Way galaxy?
What is the difference between an astronomical unit and a light year?

explain.say: The Sun is actually a star. Stars are giant balls of hot gas. They create their own light and heat.
Our Sun is a type of star called a yellow dwarf. It is very close to Earth. It provides us with much of our energy.
Our solar system is located within a galaxy. The Milky Way is our home galaxy. It is a spiral galaxy shape.
Galaxies are huge groups of stars and gas. The Milky Way contains billions of stars. Other galaxies exist too.
A light year measures distance, not time. It is the distance light travels in one year. This helps us measure far away objects.

draw.text: Light year: Distance light travels in one year

explain.say: For example, the nearest star system is about four light years away. This shows how vast space is.

draw.text: Example: Nearest star system is 4 light years away

faq.q: What is the difference between a star and a galaxy?
faq.a: A star is a single massive ball of hot gas like our Sun. A galaxy is a huge collection of billions of stars, gas, and dust.
asks: What is a galaxy made of?

faq.q: How do we measure distances in space?
faq.a: We use units like light years to measure distance across space. A light year is the distance light travels in one full year.
asks: Is a light year a unit of time?

faq.q: Is the Sun the only star we know?
faq.a: No, the Sun is just one star among billions. Our galaxy, the Milky Way, contains countless other stars.
asks: Are there other stars besides the Sun?
How many stars are in the Milky Way?

faq.a: A spiral galaxy has arms that rotate around a central point. The Milky Way galaxy has a spiral shape.
asks: What shape is the Milky Way?
What kind of galaxy has arms?

faq.q: Do all galaxies look like the Milky Way?
faq.a: No, galaxies come in different shapes. Some are spiral, some are elliptical, and some are irregular.
asks: What are the types of galaxies?

facts: Stars generate energy through nuclear fusion.
The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy.
A light year measures distance, not time.
Galaxies are massive collections of stars and gas.

quiz.say: The Sun is best described as:
quiz.why: The Sun is a massive ball of hot gas that produces its own light and heat.

wrong.0: A galaxy contains billions of stars, while the Sun is only one.
wrong.2: Planets orbit stars; they do not generate their own light.
wrong.3: Nebulae are clouds of gas where stars form, not the star itself.

quiz.say: If you measure the distance to a star, you use:
quiz.why: Light years are the standard unit for measuring vast interstellar distances.

wrong.0: Years measure time, not the physical distance across space.
wrong.2: Kilometers are too small a unit for measuring distances between stars.
wrong.3: Astronomical units measure distances within our own solar system.

quiz.say: The Milky Way is an example of which galaxy type?
quiz.why: The Milky Way is known for its distinct, rotating spiral arms.

wrong.0: A cluster is a group of galaxies, not a specific shape type.
wrong.2: Elliptical galaxies are generally rounder or more oval in shape.
wrong.3: Irregular galaxies do not fit into a clear, defined shape pattern.
